the_failure.message: KeyError: no architecture adapter registered for family 'qwen3'; registered: []. Registration is explicit: call aadistill.initialization.adapters.register_builtin_adapters() before resolving one.
the_failure.root_cause: registration stopped being an import side effect when the adapter registry became something a caller builds. The Phase-A driver, the recovery-continuation driver and six scripts all picked up the explicit call; the C1 driver did not. It loaded 398 parent weight tensors and then asked an empty registry for the qwen3 adapter.
the_failure.why_nothing_caught_it: a process-default registry is empty in a fresh process and full in a pytest session where any other test registered it. In-process coverage of the driver could not see this by construction, and stage D itself only runs on a pod with real weights. It is the seam that the extraction left unexecuted.
the_failure.repaired_by: the C1 driver calls register_builtin_adapters() at import, beside register_builtin_profiles(), matching every other driver. The C1 preflight now imports the driver in a SUBPROCESS and resolves the adapter for the family the pinned checkpoint config declares — the only form of the check a shared pytest process cannot fake. Mutating the fix away reproduces attempt 16's exact error.
the_failure.no_siblings: every other entry point that resolves an adapter already registers; the five scripts that name the adapter file do so only as a string in a frozen file list.
